claims.text: Standard processing can produce a CrFeCoNi high-entropy alloy with a clean, oxide-free surface.
Oxidizing CrFeCoNi at 400 °C for 30 minutes in a controlled oxygen-containing atmosphere will form a thin Cr2O3 surface layer.
The proposed oxidation treatment can produce a uniform and adherent Cr2O3 layer.
The Cr2O3 surface layer acts as an antiferromagnetic phase under the proposed measurement conditions.
The CrFeCoNi bulk is ferromagnetic and can form an FM/AFM interface with the Cr2O3 surface layer.
A well-adherent Cr2O3 layer establishes a robust FM/AFM interface on CrFeCoNi.
Exchange coupling can arise across an FM/AFM interface and affect exchange-bias behavior.
Exchange coupling at the Cr2O3/CrFeCoNi interface promotes additional domain-wall pinning.
The additional domain-wall pinning raises the energy barrier for magnetization reversal.
An exchange-coupled FM/AFM interface can enhance coercivity relative to an FM control.
Controlled surface oxidation of CrFeCoNi will produce a measurable and appreciable coercivity increase relative to an identically processed untreated control.
The coercivity enhancement should vanish when the system is heated above the blocking or Néel temperature.
The coercivity enhancement requires the Cr2O3 layer to have a suitable thickness, uniformity, adhesion, and antiferromagnetic stability.
An overly thick or discontinuous Cr2O3 layer could eliminate the coercivity enhancement.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement is sensitive to oxidation parameters, oxide thickness, and oxide uniformity.
Exchange bias and its associated coercivity enhancement are temperature dependent near the blocking temperature.
Temperatures below 200 K are well below the expected blocking temperature of the proposed Cr2O3/CrFeCoNi interface.
Failure of exchange bias to persist below the known Cr2O3 blocking temperature would indicate an unstable or non-uniform oxide layer.
